title: Karmathy Rule Pack
description: A rule pack is a versioned, signed, jurisdiction-specific set of statutory rules. It is the ONLY artifact in Karmathy that may contain statutory values: tax rates, minimum wage, statutory leave entitlement, notice periods, working-time limits, overtime thresholds, mandatory payslip fields and filing obligations. A pack that is not `verified` is never used in a calculation: a pack whose status is `verified` is the only one that may be used in a production payroll calculation, and a verified pack must not contain placeholder values, nulls standing in for a required number, or sentinel text. Every pack must name the legal document it was derived from in `source`, must be signed in `signing`, and must ship at least one golden case so that the engine can be regression tested against the rule. A pack applies to a single jurisdiction, identified by `jurisdiction`, and is valid between `effective_from` and `effective_to`.

pack_id.title: Pack identifier
pack_id.description: Stable slug that identifies the rule pack across the catalogue, the signing key registry and the API. It never changes once published: a corrected pack ships as a new version of the same pack_id.

name.title: Pack display name
name.description: Short title shown in the rule pack catalogue, for example the name of the jurisdiction and the coverage of the pack.

jurisdiction.title: Jurisdiction
jurisdiction.description: The jurisdiction this pack applies to. Exactly one pack may be attached to a tenant for a given jurisdiction and effective period, so the country and optional region identify the pack unambiguously.

country.title: Country code
country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country whose law the pack encodes.

region.title: Region or subdivision
region.description: ISO 3166-2 or national subdivision code within the country, used where the law differs by state, province or territory. Omit when the pack covers the whole country.

display_name.title: Jurisdiction display name
display_name.description: Human readable name of the jurisdiction as it should be shown to an administrator, for example `India - Karnataka`.

version.title: Pack version
version.description: Semantic version of the pack content. MAJOR is bumped when a rule changes in a way that alters a calculation, MINOR when rules are added, PATCH for wording and citation fixes. A tenant keeps using the version it was verified on until it explicitly migrates.

status.title: Pack status
status.description: Lifecycle state of the pack. `draft` is editable and unusable. `pending_verification` is frozen and waiting for a reviewer. `verified` is signed off against the cited source and is the only state that may drive a calculation. `superseded` is a previously verified pack that has been replaced and must not be applied to new periods.

supersedes.title: Superseded packs
supersedes.description: Pack identifiers of the packs this one replaces. The server refuses to attach two packs with overlapping effective periods for the same jurisdiction, so this list is what makes the replacement explicit.

items.title: Superseded pack identifier
items.description: Slug of the pack this one replaces.

effective_from.title: Effective from
effective_from.description: First date, inclusive, on which this pack may be applied. A pack may be attached to a tenant only for a period that starts on or after this date.

effective_to.title: Effective to
effective_to.description: Last date, inclusive, on which this pack may be applied, or null when the pack has no end date. It must be greater than or equal to `effective_from`; the server enforces that ordering.

tz.title: Time zone
tz.description: IANA time zone identifier of the jurisdiction, used for cut-off times, pay day calculations, public holiday dates and the interpretation of local timestamps. It must be the zone the statute refers to, not the tenant's preferred display zone.

source.title: Source
source.description: The legal instrument the rules were derived from. A pack with no source cannot leave `draft`: the server refuses to move a pack to `pending_verification` unless the source names a document, its publisher and its reference.

document_title.title: Document title
document_title.description: Full title of the legal instrument, for example the name of the Act, Ordinance, Code or notification the rules come from.

publisher.title: Publisher
publisher.description: The government department, ministry or regulator that published the document.

document_reference.title: Document reference
document_reference.description: The citation of the instrument: Act number, rule number, notification number, gazette reference or section numbers. This is the value a reviewer checks against the source, so it must be specific enough to locate the provision.

url.title: Source URL
url.description: Link to the published document, or null when the instrument is only available in print or is not published online.

retrieved_on.title: Retrieved on
retrieved_on.description: Date the source document was last consulted. The server warns when this is more than a year before the pack's verification date, because the instrument may have been amended.

notes.title: Source notes
notes.description: Anything the reviewer needs to know about the source: amendments, translation, conflicting provisions, or the reason a provision was interpreted a particular way.

verification.title: Verification
verification.description: The reviewer sign-off that made this pack trustworthy, or null while the pack is still a draft. It is required, complete, and non-null once the status is `verified`. A verification record is not a substitute for the pack being signed: both are needed.

verified_by_name.title: Verified by
verified_by_name.description: Full name of the person who checked the rules against the cited source and against the golden cases.

verified_by_role.title: Verifier role
verified_by_role.description: The verifier's role, for example `payroll compliance analyst` or `external counsel`. Recorded so that the weight of a verification can be judged later.

verified_on.title: Verified on
verified_on.description: Date the verification was performed. The server requires it to be on or after the date the source was retrieved.

source_document_reference.title: Verified source reference
source_document_reference.description: The document reference the reviewer actually checked, which may be more specific than `source.document_reference`, for example the exact section and the amendment that applied on the effective date.

golden_case_set_id.title: Golden case set identifier
golden_case_set_id.description: Identifier of the golden case set the pack was verified against. It must resolve to the cases shipped in `golden_cases` and must not be empty: a rule cannot be verified without at least one golden case.

rate_tables.title: Rate tables
rate_tables.description: Named tables of statutory rates, keyed by table name. Table names are the stable join key used by the payroll engine, for example a table of progressive tax bands or a table of social insurance contribution ceilings. This is one of only two places in the product where statutory numbers may live, the other being `thresholds`.

propertyNames.title: Rate table name
propertyNames.description: Key of a rate table, used by the calculation engine to find the table.

thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.description: Statutory numeric thresholds for the jurisdiction. Every value here is statutory and jurisdiction-specific: it is not a company policy and it may not be set by a tenant. A null value means the jurisdiction sets no such threshold, and it is never a stand-in for a value that was simply not filled in. The server rejects a verified pack that still contains a null in a field the jurisdiction does define.

weekly_max_hours.title: Maximum weekly hours
weekly_max_hours.description: Statutory ceiling on hours an employee may work in a week, or null where the jurisdiction sets no ceiling. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

daily_min_rest_hours.title: Minimum daily rest hours
daily_min_rest_hours.description: Statutory minimum uninterrupted rest between two work periods in a day, or null where the jurisdiction sets no minimum rest. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

max_consecutive_work_days.title: Maximum consecutive work days
max_consecutive_work_days.description: Statutory maximum number of consecutive days an employee may be rostered to work, or null where the jurisdiction sets no such limit. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

daily_overtime_threshold_hours.title: Daily overtime threshold
daily_overtime_threshold_hours.description: Statutory number of hours worked in a day after which overtime is payable, or null where overtime is only triggered weekly. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

weekly_overtime_threshold_hours.title: Weekly overtime threshold
weekly_overtime_threshold_hours.description: Statutory number of hours worked in a week after which overtime is payable, or null where the jurisdiction sets no weekly overtime threshold. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

overtime_premium_multiplier.title: Overtime premium multiplier
overtime_premium_multiplier.description: Statutory multiple applied to the normal rate to pay overtime, for example the factor applied to an hour of normal pay, or null where the jurisdiction has no premium. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

overtime_daily_cap_hours.title: Daily overtime cap
overtime_daily_cap_hours.description: Statutory maximum number of overtime hours payable in a single day, or null where there is no cap. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

minimum_wage_amount.title: Minimum wage amount
minimum_wage_amount.description: Statutory minimum wage for the unit given in `minimum_wage_unit`, expressed in the currency of the jurisdiction, or null where the jurisdiction fixes no statutory minimum wage. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

minimum_wage_unit.title: Minimum wage unit
minimum_wage_unit.description: The period the minimum wage is expressed per, for example `per_hour`, `per_day`, `per_month` or `per_pay_period`, or null when there is no statutory minimum wage. A free string so that a jurisdiction with an unusual unit can still be expressed; the engine reads the unit, it does not assume one.

overtime.title: Overtime
overtime.description: Statutory overtime rules for the jurisdiction. The thresholds are mirrored in `thresholds` so that a single field can be read without walking the whole pack; the values in the two places must agree and the server rejects a pack where they do not.

daily_threshold_hours.title: Daily overtime threshold
daily_threshold_hours.description: Hours worked in a day after which overtime is payable, or null when the jurisdiction has no daily overtime threshold. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

weekly_threshold_hours.title: Weekly overtime threshold
weekly_threshold_hours.description: Hours worked in a week after which overtime is payable, or null when the jurisdiction has no weekly overtime threshold. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

premium_multiplier.title: Overtime premium multiplier
premium_multiplier.description: Statutory multiple applied to the normal rate when paying overtime, or null where the jurisdiction has no premium. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

daily_cap_hours.title: Daily overtime cap
daily_cap_hours.description: Maximum overtime hours payable in one day, or null where there is no cap. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

rules.title: Overtime compliance rules
rules.description: The individual overtime provisions of the jurisdiction, each of which can be reported as a blocking or advisory finding on a timesheet or a pay run.

leave_types.title: Leave types
leave_types.description: The statutory leave types the jurisdiction grants, with entitlement, accrual, carry-over and encashment. These are the authoritative values for the tenant; a preset may only name the leave types it wants and must leave the numbers to this pack.

working_time_limits.title: Working time limits
working_time_limits.description: Statutory limits on how much and how often an employee may work. Every limit is jurisdiction-specific; a null means the jurisdiction sets no such limit, not that the value was forgotten.

max_weekly_hours.title: Maximum weekly hours
max_weekly_hours.description: Statutory ceiling on hours worked per week, or null where the jurisdiction sets no ceiling. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

min_daily_rest_hours.title: Minimum daily rest hours
min_daily_rest_hours.description: Statutory minimum rest between two work periods in a day, or null where the jurisdiction sets no minimum rest. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

max_consecutive_days.title: Maximum consecutive work days
max_consecutive_days.description: Statutory maximum number of consecutive days an employee may work, or null where the jurisdiction sets no limit. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

max_night_work_hours.title: Maximum night work hours
max_night_work_hours.description: Statutory maximum number of night hours an employee may work, or null where the jurisdiction sets no night work limit. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

min_rest_between_shifts_hours.title: Minimum rest between shifts
min_rest_between_shifts_hours.description: Statutory minimum rest between the end of one shift and the start of the next, or null where the jurisdiction sets no such minimum. Statutory and jurisdiction-specific.

rules.title: Working time compliance rules
rules.description: The individual working-time provisions of the jurisdiction, each of which can be reported as a blocking or advisory finding on a roster or a timesheet.

break_rules.title: Break rules
break_rules.description: Statutory break entitlements: how long a break must be, when it must be taken and whether it is paid. These are the values a preset's `time.break_rules` defer to.

mandatory_payslip_fields.title: Mandatory payslip fields
mandatory_payslip_fields.description: Field names that a payslip produced in this jurisdiction MUST contain, for example `gross_pay`, `net_pay`, `employer_contributions` or `hours_worked`. The server refuses to generate a payslip that omits any of them and the payslip template is checked against this list on every pay run.

items.title: Mandatory payslip field
items.description: Name of a field that the payslip must contain, in the canonical payslip field vocabulary.

mandatory_payslip_notes.title: Mandatory payslip notes
mandatory_payslip_notes.description: Optional list of literal statements that must appear on a payslip, for example a right-to-retain or right-to-query notice. The text is reproduced verbatim, so it must be written as the law requires it to be shown.

items.title: Mandatory payslip note
items.description: One statement that must be printed on every payslip, reproduced verbatim.

pay_frequency_rules.title: Pay frequency rules
pay_frequency_rules.description: The pay cycle the jurisdiction permits and how the pay date is derived. The server refuses to enable payroll for a tenant whose preset frequency is not in `allowed_frequencies`.

allowed_frequencies.title: Allowed pay frequencies
allowed_frequencies.description: The pay frequencies that are lawful in this jurisdiction. A tenant's preset must choose one of these, or payroll enablement is refused.

items.title: Allowed pay frequency
items.description: One of the pay frequencies that are lawful in this jurisdiction.

pay_day_rule.title: Pay day rule
pay_day_rule.description: Plain English statement of how the pay date is determined, for example the last working day of the month or a fixed day, and how public holidays shift it.

cut_off_days_before_pay_day.title: Cut-off days before pay day
cut_off_days_before_pay_day.description: Number of days before the pay day on which timesheets and changes must be submitted for the period to be paid on time.

pay_date_rule_id.title: Pay date rule identifier
pay_date_rule_id.description: Stable identifier of the pay-date computation rule the engine implements, for example a named rule for the last working day of the month. It is referenced by the calculation engine and by the audit trail.

reporting_obligations.title: Reporting obligations
reporting_obligations.description: The statutory returns the employer in this jurisdiction must file, with their frequency, deadline and authority. The server uses this list to drive the compliance calendar and to warn before a deadline is missed.

public_holiday_rules.title: Public holiday rules
public_holiday_rules.description: How public holidays are determined in this jurisdiction, and whether the holiday calendar differs by region.

source.title: Public holiday source
source.description: The authority and instrument that publishes the public holiday list, and the date the list for each year was last retrieved.

region_dependent.title: Region dependent
region_dependent.description: Whether the public holiday list differs by region within the jurisdiction. When true, the holiday calendar for a location is resolved from the region's own list rather than from the national one.

holiday_count_by_year.title: Holiday count by year
holiday_count_by_year.description: Number of public holidays in each year, keyed by four digit year. The engine uses it to sanity check the holiday calendar that is loaded for a year; the calendar itself is held as tenant data, not in the pack.

propertyNames.title: Year
propertyNames.description: Four digit calendar year the holiday count belongs to.

additionalProperties.title: Holiday count
additionalProperties.description: Number of public holidays in that year.

signing.title: Signing
signing.description: The signature over the pack. A pack MUST be signed to be usable: the server rejects an unsigned pack before it may drive a calculation, and it rejects a pack whose signature does not verify against the registered public key for `key_id`. The signature covers the canonical JSON serialisation of the pack with this block removed.

algorithm.title: Signature algorithm
algorithm.description: The signature algorithm. Ed25519 is the only accepted algorithm; a pack signed with anything else is rejected.

key_id.title: Key identifier
key_id.description: Identifier of the signing key in the trust registry. The server looks the key up here to verify the signature and to prove the pack was signed by a known key.

signature.title: Signature
signature.description: The base64 encoded signature bytes. It must be the signature over the canonical form of the pack as described in the signing block description.

signed_at.title: Signed at
signed_at.description: UTC timestamp, RFC 3339 with an explicit offset, at which the pack was signed. A signature timestamped before the source was retrieved is rejected, because the sign-off cannot have covered the cited document.

signed_by.title: Signed by
signed_by.description: Identity of the signer, for example the release pipeline or the compliance lead who authorised the pack.

golden_cases.title: Golden cases
golden_cases.description: Worked examples that pin the expected output of the rules in this pack. A rule cannot be verified without at least one golden case, and the server refuses to move a pack to `verified` while `golden_cases` is empty. Each case states an input and the expected result; the regression suite replays every case of every verified pack on every engine change.

allOf.title: Verified pack requirements
allOf.description: A pack may only be marked `verified` when it names the reviewer, cites the source the reviewer checked, names the golden case set it was verified against and ships at least one golden case. The same conditions must hold for the pack to drive a production payroll calculation.

if.title: When the pack status is verified

status.title: Status under test
status.description: The pack status being tested by this conditional.

then.title: What a verified pack must carry
then.description: The verification record must be present, must be an object rather than null, must carry all of its fields, and must name a non-empty golden case set. At least one golden case must be shipped.

verification.title: Verification record
verification.description: The verification record of a verified pack. It must be an object, never null, and it must carry every field listed in its required list.

golden_case_set_id.title: Golden case set identifier
golden_case_set_id.description: Must name a non-empty golden case set that resolves to the cases shipped in this pack.

golden_cases.title: Golden cases
golden_cases.description: A verified pack must ship at least one golden case: a rule cannot be verified without one.

allOf.title: Superseded pack end date
allOf.description: A pack that has been replaced must state the date on which it stopped applying, so that historical periods are still resolved to the pack that was in force at the time.

if.title: When the pack status is superseded

status.title: Status under test
status.description: The pack status being tested by this conditional.

then.title: What a superseded pack must carry
then.description: The pack must carry a non-null end date.

effective_to.title: Effective to
effective_to.description: The date on which the superseded pack stopped applying. It must be an ISO date, never null.

json_value.title: Arbitrary JSON value
json_value.description: Any JSON value. Used only where the contract genuinely cannot constrain the shape, for example inside a golden case input or expected result.

anyOf.title: Null value
anyOf.description: An explicit null, used where a value is present but unset.

anyOf.title: Array value
anyOf.description: An ordered list whose members are themselves arbitrary JSON values.

anyOf.title: Object value
anyOf.description: A map whose members are themselves arbitrary JSON values.

compliance_rule.title: Compliance rule
compliance_rule.description: A single statutory provision, expressed so that the engine can evaluate it and report on it. `severity` decides whether a breach blocks the action: a `block` rule stops the timesheet, the roster or the pay run, a `flag` rule produces a warning that a human may override with a recorded reason.

rule_id.title: Rule identifier
rule_id.description: Stable identifier of the rule, referenced from leave types, break rules and audit findings. It must be unique inside the pack.

description.title: Rule description
description.description: Plain English statement of the rule and the consequence of breaching it, as an administrator would read it.

severity.title: Severity
severity.description: Whether a breach blocks the operation or is advisory.

applies_when.title: Applies when
applies_when.description: The condition under which the rule is evaluated, written as a human readable predicate over the payroll or timesheet facts, for example when the employee is classified as a night worker or when the weekly hours exceed the threshold.

rate_entry.title: Rate table entry
rate_entry.description: One row of a rate table, used when the table is a list of bands or schedules. The table says which of the two it is, in its `kind`, and the two rows are not the same shape. A row of a band table states three numbers: `value`, the lower bound of the band; `max_value`, its upper bound; and `rate`, the percentage rate that applies inside the band. Every band of a banded table states all three: the schema refuses a banded table that leaves the rate out of one of its bands, so the pack is rejected when it is loaded rather than when a pay run needs the figure. A row of a schedule table states a value and a unit and carries no rate of its own. The bounds are expressed in the stated `unit`; the rate is a percentage whatever that unit is, so a bound is never read as a rate and a rate is never read as a bound. The engine divides the taxable amount between the bands by their bounds and taxes each part at the rate of the band it falls in.

code.title: Entry code
code.description: Stable code of the entry within the table, used as the lookup key by the calculation engine.

label.title: Entry label
label.description: Human readable label of the band or rate, as it should be shown in a breakdown.

value.title: Value
value.description: The statutory value of the entry in the stated unit. For a band table this is the lower bound of the band: the amount at which the band starts. The engine reads it as a bound and never as a rate; the rate of the band is the band's own `rate`.

max_value.title: Maximum value
max_value.description: Upper bound of the band, omitted for an open ended top band. The bound is exclusive: the band covers the amount from `value` up to, but not including, `max_value`.

rate.title: Band rate
rate.description: The percentage rate that applies inside this band, expressed in percent, so 5 means 5 %. It is the only number in the row that is a rate, and it is a percentage whatever the unit of the bounds is. Every band of a banded table states it, and the schema refuses a banded table whose bands leave it out; the engine refuses a pack whose band table leaves the rate out rather than guess one, because a wrong pay figure is worse than a refusal. A row of a schedule table states no rate of its own.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The unit the bounds of the entry are expressed in. A free string so that any jurisdiction can be expressed; the common units are `currency_amount`, `per_hour`, `per_day`, `per_month` and `per_year`. The rate of the band is always a percentage and is not expressed in this unit.

notes.title: Entry notes
notes.description: Anything the reader needs to understand the band, for example the condition under which it applies or a citation of the provision.

rate_value.title: Rate table value
rate_value.description: One value of a rate table that is expressed as a keyed map rather than as a list of entries. The map key is the code the engine looks up.

value.title: Value
value.description: The statutory value for this key in the stated unit.

unit.title: Unit
unit.description: The unit the value is expressed in. A free string; the common units are `percent`, `currency_amount`, `per_hour`, `per_day`, `per_month` and `per_year`.

label.title: Label
label.description: Human readable label of the entry, when the key alone is not self explanatory.

notes.title: Notes
notes.description: Anything the reader needs to understand the entry, for example a citation of the provision it comes from.

rate_table.title: Rate table
rate_table.description: A named table of statutory rates. It is written either as a list of `entries` or as a keyed map of `values`, never both, so that the engine always reads one shape. A table written as a list of rows also says what shape those rows have, in `kind`: `banded` for a progressive table whose rows are bands, and `schedule` for a table whose rows are scheduled values that carry no rate of their own. The two forms are read differently and are never read as one another: a banded table (`entries`) states, for every band, the amount at which the band starts, the amount at which it ends and the rate that applies inside it; a flat map (`values`) states, for every code, a single percentage rate that applies to the whole base. The table applies from `effective_from`; a table that changed mid-year is expressed as two tables with different effective dates.

description.title: Table description
description.description: What the table contains and how it is applied, for example the progressive bands applied to taxable monthly pay.

effective_from.title: Effective from
effective_from.description: First date on which this table applies. A rate change mid-year is expressed as a new table.

kind.title: Table kind
kind.description: The shape of the rows of a table that is written as a list of `entries`. `banded` for a progressive table whose rows are bands: each band states the amount at which it starts, the amount at which it ends and the rate that applies inside it, and a banded table has to state that rate on every one of its bands. `schedule` for a table whose rows are scheduled values: each row states a value and a unit and carries no rate of its own, so the schema asks it for none. A table written as a keyed map has no rows and declares no kind.

entries.title: Table entries
entries.description: The rows of the table, in ascending order of value. Use this form for banded or scheduled rates, and say which of the two it is in `kind`. The engine reads `value` as the lower bound of the band, `max_value` as its upper bound and `rate` as the percentage rate that applies inside the band, and it divides the taxable amount between the bands by those bounds.

values.title: Table values
values.description: The values of the table as a map from code to value. Use this form for a flat lookup such as a set of ceilings by category. The map is deliberately open: its keys are the codes the engine looks up. The engine reads `value` as a percentage rate that applies to the whole base, whatever the code means.

propertyNames.title: Rate code
propertyNames.description: Key of the value in the table, as the engine looks it up.

oneOf.title: Entries form
oneOf.description: The table is a list of rows and says what shape those rows have.

not.title: Not a keyed map as well
not.description: A table is written in one form or the other, never in both.

oneOf.title: Keyed map form
oneOf.description: The table is a map of code to value. A map has no rows, so it declares no kind.

not.title: Neither rows nor a kind
not.description: A map is not a list of rows, and a table in the map form declares no kind.

allOf.title: A banded table states a rate on every band
allOf.description: A banded table's rows are bands. A band states the amount at which it starts, the amount at which it ends and the rate that applies inside it, and a band that leaves the rate out cannot be calculated. The schema refuses such a pack when it is loaded, rather than leaving the gap to be discovered when a pay run needs the figure.

if.title: When the table declares itself banded

kind.title: Kind under test
kind.description: The kind of the table being tested by this conditional.

then.title: What a banded table must carry
then.description: The table has to be a list of rows, and every one of its bands has to state the rate that applies inside it.

entries.title: Bands of a banded table
entries.description: Every band of a banded table states the rate that applies inside it.

items.title: A band of a banded table
items.description: A band of a banded table. It states the rate that applies inside it, and the schema refuses a banded table whose bands leave the rate out.

allOf.title: A schedule table's rows carry no rate
allOf.description: A schedule table's rows are scheduled values: each row states a value and a unit and no rate of its own, so the schema does not ask a schedule table for a rate.

if.title: When the table declares itself a schedule

kind.title: Kind under test
kind.description: The kind of the table being tested by this conditional.

then.title: What a schedule table must carry
then.description: The table has to be a list of rows, and its rows are not asked for a rate.

tenure_tier.title: Tenure tier
tenure_tier.description: A length-of-service band that grants a different leave entitlement. Tiers are evaluated in ascending order of `after_years` and the first band whose threshold the employee has reached applies.

after_years.title: Years of service threshold
after_years.description: Length of service, in whole years, at which the tier starts. Zero means the tier applies from day one.

days.title: Entitlement days
days.description: Days of leave the tier grants per year. This is a statutory number.

accrual.title: Accrual
accrual.description: How the entitlement is earned over the leave year. This is the statutory accrual rule for the jurisdiction and it overrides anything a preset or a tenant says.

frequency.title: Accrual frequency
frequency.description: How often leave accrues. `front_loaded` means the whole entitlement is credited at the start of the leave year.

tenure_tiers.title: Tenure tiers
tenure_tiers.description: Length-of-service bands with their own entitlement. May be empty when the entitlement does not vary with tenure.

leave_type.title: Leave type
leave_type.description: A statutory leave type and the entitlement it grants. The `code` is the join key a preset must use for the same leave type.

code.title: Leave type code
code.description: Stable slug of the leave type, used to join the pack with the tenant's leave configuration.

name.title: Leave type name
name.description: Statutory name of the leave, for example the name the law itself uses.

entitlement_days.title: Entitlement days
entitlement_days.description: Days of leave granted per leave year under this type. This is a statutory number and it must be present.

accrual.title: Accrual
accrual.description: How the entitlement is earned over the leave year.

carry_over_limit_days.title: Carry-over limit
carry_over_limit_days.description: Days of unused leave that may be carried into the next leave year. Zero means that no leave may be carried over.

expiry_month.title: Expiry month
expiry_month.description: Month, 1 to 12, in which unused leave expires.

encashable.title: Encashable
encashable.description: Whether the employee has a right to have unused leave paid out. A statutory right, not a company policy.

entitlement_source.title: Entitlement source
entitlement_source.description: Text citing the provision the entitlement comes from, for example the section and schedule of the instrument named in `source`. A reviewer reads this to confirm the entitlement was taken from the law and not from another pack.

rule_ids.title: Related rule identifiers
rule_ids.description: Identifiers of the compliance rules that apply to this leave type, for example a rule that caps consecutive sick days.

items.title: Related rule identifier
items.description: Identifier of a compliance rule that applies to this leave type.

break_rule.title: Break rule
break_rule.description: A statutory break entitlement: how many hours must be worked before a break must be taken, how long that break is and whether it is paid.

after_hours.title: After hours
after_hours.description: Hours of continuous work after which the break must be taken, or null where the entitlement does not depend on how long the employee has worked.

duration_minutes.title: Duration
duration_minutes.description: Length of the break in minutes, or null where the law does not fix a length.

paid.title: Paid
paid.description: Whether the break is paid time.

rule_id.title: Rule identifier
rule_id.description: Identifier of the compliance rule that this break entitlement implements.

description.title: Description
description.description: Plain English statement of the break entitlement and how it is enforced in the product.

reporting_obligation.title: Reporting obligation
reporting_obligation.description: A statutory return the employer must file, with the authority that receives it and the deadline it is due by.

report_id.title: Report identifier
report_id.description: Stable identifier of the obligation, used to key the compliance calendar and to deduplicate obligations across pack versions.

name.title: Report name
name.description: Name of the return as the authority calls it.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.description: How often the return must be filed.

due_within_days.title: Due within days
due_within_days.description: Number of days after the end of the reporting period within which the return must be filed.

template_ref.title: Template reference
template_ref.description: Reference to the statutory template or schema the return must follow, or null when the authority accepts a free-form return.

authority.title: Authority
authority.description: The government body or agency the return is filed with.

description.title: Description
description.description: What the return covers, which data the product must collect for it and any note the administrator needs.

golden_case.title: Golden case
golden_case.description: A worked example that pins the expected behaviour of the rules. `input` and `expected` are deliberately open maps: the shape of the facts and of the result is defined by the rule the case exercises, not by this contract. The case is replayed by the regression suite and a mismatch fails the build.

case_id.title: Case identifier
case_id.description: Identifier of the case within the pack. It must be unique inside the pack and is referenced by the verification record's golden case set.

description.title: Case description
description.description: What the case exercises and why it was chosen, for example a worker on the lowest pay band working the maximum permitted hours.

input.title: Case input
input.description: The facts fed to the engine. Open map: the keys are the facts the exercised rule reads and the values are arbitrary JSON.

expected.title: Expected result
expected.description: The result the engine must produce for the given input. Open map: the keys are the outputs the exercised rule produces and the values are arbitrary JSON.
